request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The rollup audit lines are in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works:** the app only ever worked out each person's claimed and due-total in the browser, so the server had nothing to compare. I added a server-side `Rollup` service (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/Rollup.java`) that does the same calculation the people screen does.

Each change first records the figures as they were. After writing its own audit line, it records them again and writes:
- a `ROLLUP` line for each person whose claimed or due-total moved, in the order people were added. A newly added person always gets one.
- a `TOTALS` line, but only if the sheet's claimed-total or due-total moved.

These lines are only written if the change goes through, so a refused change still writes nothing.

**Where it's hooked in:** adding and editing a person, setting a rate, adding and editing a claim, opening, settling and voiding a claim, taking a statement, and changing the sheet's today. Changing today had no audit line before, and still has none of its own. To record who made that change, the today endpoint now passes the signed-in user to the service.

**One difference from the request:** the request's wording is `ROLLUP name=<name> …`, but the spec expects `ROLLUP sheet=<id> by=<user> person=<name> claimed=… due-total=…`. I followed the spec, so the field is `person=`, not `name=`.

The screen and stored data are unchanged.
